nodes.question: What are the three main areas of research on the carbon footprint of air tourism?
nodes.answer: The three main areas of research are the quantification of CO2 emissions, technological innovations and emission reduction strategies, and carbon policies and offsets.
nodes.paragraph: Research on the carbon footprint of air tourism can be grouped into three main areas: (1) Quantification of CO2 Emissions: studies that aim to formulate measurement strate - gies, quantifying air tourism emissions are crucial to understand their environmental impact, as well as to achieve an effective management of emissions with the aim of mitigating them (Becken and Hay 2007; Luo et al. 2010; Sharp et al. 2016; Wang et al 2017 ; Lezen et al. 2018 ; Rico et al. 2019; Antequera et al. 2021 ; Huang and Tang 2021 ; Li et al. 2023; UNWTO 2023; Conefrey and Hanrahan 2024). (2) Technological innovations and emission reduction strategies are key to addressing the challenge of reducing the carbon footprint (Peeters et al. 2006; Bows et al. 2009; Langhans and Gollnick 2009; Upham et al. 2009; Peeters 2010; Wolters et al. 2014; Lee et al. 2021; Nathaniel et al. 2023; Peng and Zhu 2023; Shehab et al. 2023; Radulovi 2024; Song et al.

nodes.question: What is the primary goal of the proposed policy by the Spanish government regarding domestic flights?
nodes.answer: The primary goal is to restrict domestic flights on routes where there is a rail alternative available with a duration of less than 2.5 hours, aiming to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

Notably, the incorporation of the aviation industry into the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading System (EU-ETS) aimed to address these emissions, covering all flights within the EU (Mu and Tao 2023). Moreover, the Updated analysis of the non-CO2 effects of aviation report (European Com- mission 2020a, b) shows that the combined non-CO2 climate impacts from aviation activities are at least as important as those of CO2 alone. In the case of Spain, studies have highlighted the impor - tance of addressing aviation emissions. Research has shown that aviation emissions have been a significant contributor to the country S total emissions, with the electricity sector also playing a substantial role (Cruz-P rez et al. 2021). Efforts to mitigate aviation emissions in Spain have included exploring alternative fuels and biofuels (Gegg et al. 2014; Filimonau et al. 2018). In this context, the government pact between the PSOE and Sumar parties for the current legislature includes a spe- cific measure for aviation. This pact, presented on 24 Octo- ber 2023, includes in Section "Discussion and conclusions" Guaranteeing the right to housing and quality transport for all that, as other neighbouring countries have done, the reduction of domestic flights on those routes where there is a rail alternative with a duration of less than 2.5 h will be promoted (PSOE y Sumar 2023).

nodes.question: What is the primary aim of the proposed policy discussed in the study?
nodes.answer: The primary aim of the proposed policy is to restrict domestic flights on routes where there is a rail alternative available with a duration of less than 2.5 hours, in order to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote more environmentally friendly transportation options.
nodes.paragraph: Research by Zhang and Nie (2021) in China demonstrated that the introduction of high-speed rail signifi - cantly decreased local carbon emissions. Similarly, a study by D Alfonso et al. (2016) highlighted that the energy con- sumption of high-speed rail which is electric is much lower than diesel trains due to the higher technical efficiency of electric trains. Moreover, the different operating conditions (fewer stops, i.e. less energy used for acceleration) make the high-speed rail even more efficient. This measure is very much in line with the current invest- ment in the national high-speed train line, both in increasing the number of routes and in improving the efficiency of the trains (RENFE 2024 ). The development of the high-speed train has been one of the government S main axes and will continue to be so as stated in the Mobility Plan 2030, in line with the EU Commission S Trans-European Transport Net- work (TEN-T) project (European Commission 2019; ADIF 2021 ; MTMS 2021 ). Moreover, the current Spanish high- speed network has proven to be particularly efficient (MTMS 2023; ADIF 2024a).

P rez Romero2,3 Martha Beatriz Flores Romero5 Accepted: 4 February 2025 The Author(s) 2025 Abstract Tourism in Mexico contributes to GDP and employment, but has environmental costs in terms of carbon emissions from air transport. The estimation of the carbon footprint of tourists arriving by air is crucial to raise awareness among decision makers in order to establish future tourism policies that reduce environmental degradation. This study esti- mates the carbon footprint generated by flights from three major Mexican tourist desti- - nations Canc n, Los Cabos, and Puerto Vallarta during the years 2022 and 2023. To carry out this research, official databases were used to determine the number of flights and the number of passengers visiting these places. Additionally, tools such as the ICAO carbon emissions calculator were employed to ensure accuracy in estimating emissions, considering factors such as flight distance, aircraft type, and passenger load.

nodes.question: What are the three main areas of research on the carbon footprint of air tourism?
nodes.answer: The three main areas of research are: (1) Quantification of CO2 emissions to understand their environmental impact and manage them effectively; (2) Technological innovations and emission reduction strategies to address carbon footprint challenges; and (3) Carbon policies and offsets that are necessary for mitigating these environmental impacts.
nodes.paragraph: Specifically, the carbon footprint of global tourism is a major concern, contributing approximately 8% of global greenhouse gas emissions, with a footprint that increased from 3.9 to 4.5 GtCO2e (Gigatonnes of Carbon Dioxide Equivalent) between 2009 and 2013 (Lenzen et al. 2018). The main contributor to the carbon footprint is transport, with air travel alone accounting for around 12% of the carbon footprint of tourism (Lenzen et al. 2018). The pandemic led to a significant decrease in tourism- related emissions in 2020, highlighting the potential for sustainable practices in the post-COVID era (Tsutsumi et al. 2024). Therefore, it is clear that the growth of tourism in Mexico entails a significant environmental cost due to the high dependence on air transport to access its main tourist destinations. In this regard, the carbon footprint of international flights to its tourist destinations is a growing concern that highlights the need for sustainable tourism policies in Mexico. It is a fact that tourism can drive economic growth, but that it also poses environmen- tal challenges that require sustainable practices to mitigate, among many other things, its carbon footprint.
